FRAME FORMAT: Deliver one continuous opaque 1024 × 3072 pixel north-up overhead environment concept master, even dimensions, fixed proportional scale from bottom to top. One unbroken map, no panels, no labels. Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: PREVIEW ONLY extension concept for the existing Bullets of Fury 16-bit vertical shooter.
STYLE REFERENCE: the supplied current native game frame establishes its biome, material colors, outline strength and overhead camera. Do not copy the small visible aircraft or HUD. Elevate its scenery into a geographically believable sequence while retaining its authored biome. Authentic detailed 1990s arcade pixel art, hard pixel clusters, dark contours and controlled dithering; not modern 3D, not blurry painting, not isometric diamond tiles.
The player travels BOTTOM TO TOP. Every section must physically connect: roads meet roads at identical width and heading, rivers have upstream/downstream continuity, bridge decks span real banks, shorelines curve gradually, terrain and lighting stay consistent at section boundaries. No horizontal seam or abruptly swapped backdrop. There is no horizon or shrinking into the distance. Keep useful open space and darker quiet masses so native aircraft, bullets and warning colors stay readable. Architectural props that could be destructible are discrete and separated from the ground.
ENVIRONMENT ONLY: no aircraft, enemies, bosses, people, vehicles, weapons, projectiles, HUD, icons, arrows, text, labels, border or watermark. Concepts propose future art, not new game mechanics.
STAGE 2 — preserve the current orange/red flowing LAVA, black/brown volcanic rock, volcanic mountain destination and open-lava boss region. Sequence bottom: cooled broken lava plains and abandoned mining access; then a small geothermal extraction compound with connected service road, pipes and low buildings; then a narrow rocky gorge crossed by one actual steel service bridge over a lava channel; then a wide broken industrial caldera perimeter with a relay foundation near a volcanic mouth; TOP: the mountain/plant edge drops behind us into an expansive uninterrupted lava sea for the native Furnace Tyrant encounter. The same magma streams run downhill through the plant and gorge. The bridge has real approaches on both banks. Open molten spans alternate with darker solid land and discrete industrial structures. Do not turn this into desert or a generic mine; lava remains unmistakable throughout. No boss baked into the art.

Match the game's authored dimensional HD 16-bit cinematic art: deliberate hard pixel clusters, dark contours, metallic highlights, crisp architecture and strong foreground/midground/background staging. STORY BEAT: the first recovered orbital recording after Stage1. Show a great communication satellite's dish/relay boom above the blue Earth limb, drawing its established metalwork, white dish and blue solar panels from the reference. A black-purple rift is opening just behind the satellite, mostly out of view. Thin black/magenta synthetic tendrils and red-magenta code-like light have begun creeping along actual dish struts and cable ports, with a few red uplink lights travelling toward Earth's night-side network below. The relay is visibly being corrupted, but the intruder's BODY AND FACE remain UNSEEN: do not draw the monster from the old reference, a skull, UFO, dragon, pilot, spacecraft or new alien character. The mystery is more effective if the threat is only its trace. Low orbital 3/4 cinematic camera, satellite in foreground right, curving blue Earth below left, hard black space and an ominous barely seen rupture above. Readable cause-and-effect: signal infrastructure is the doorway. Restrained magenta/red contamination against clean blue-white human technology.
